dossier.public_summary: A small 5441 ppm flat-bottomed dip repeats every 1.38 days for 61 transits on the target M dwarf with no odd/even difference or secondary and no nearby star able to mimic it, consistent with a ~2 Earth-radius planet. The duration is longer than expected for the star’s density and there is strong spot-driven out-of-transit variability, so follow-up spectroscopy is needed to confirm the orbit, but a blended binary or spots-driven false alarm is ruled out by the centroid and stability checks.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target; all neighbours that could fake the dip are ruled out (closest suspect 37.2 sigma away), and plausible_within_1px=0
Transit depth implies a ~2 Earth-radius planet, well below the star size regime, on a 0.2511 Rsun M dwarf at 13.78 Tmag
Flat-bottomed transit (negative V signature) with fit_b 0.01329 central impact parameter favours planet over grazing EB
No odd/even difference and secondary.snr 2.593 (best_brightening_snr 16.75) no secondary dip; period_x2=2.76 shows no EB at twice period
Depth steady across 4 sectors and 61 transits with low top-3 share, not driven by few events or by a nearby star’s contamination, and sector_depths_by_source not needed (p>0.01)
